h1:
Breakfast Like an Uttaradit Local
Morning Market, Khao Phan Phak, Old-School Coffee
intro: If you want to get to know Uttaradit fast, get up early and go eat with the locals. The town wakes up quietly, but the breakfast scene is fuller than you'd expect. There's the morning market with fresh patongko and hot soy milk, khao phan phak — Laplae's signature dish that's been around for over a century — clay-pot congee that opens at 5am, and strong old-school coffee where the old regulars still hold their usual seats. We've picked the spots people in Uttaradit actually go to, with prices and opening hours we've checked.

blocks.html: Uttaradit isn't a tourist town packed on every corner, but that's exactly the charm of breakfast here. Most places are run by locals, prices are down-to-earth, and there are local dishes that are hard to find anywhere else — especially khao phan phak from Laplae, which counts as the provincial dish. If you've only got one morning, split it into two parts: walk the morning market in town first, then drive out to Laplae to hunt down khao phan phak.

blocks.text: Start the Day at the Morning Market

blocks.html: The heart of breakfast in Uttaradit is Khlong Pho Market in the municipal area of Tha It subdistrict. The main market gets busy in the evening, but the breakfast side has stalls open from around 5:30am. You can graze your way through fresh-fried patongko, hot soy milk, grilled sticky rice with banana, taro, sweet potato, bamboo shoots, durian (in season), and old-style rice porridge.

items: Thikamporn Soy Milk — a Khlong Pho Market regular with real fresh milk and fresh-fried patongko, a light breakfast people grab before work.

Pa Phon's Grilled Sticky Rice & Old-Style Khanom Wong — a long-running stall in Khlong Pho Market with generously filled grilled sticky rice and crispy fried khanom wong rings that are hard to find in other towns now.
Grab-and-go breakfast bites — khanom jeen with curry sauce, rice porridge, Thai sweets, local drinks. You can browse several stalls in one loop.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: Breakfast at Khlong Pho Market is best between 6:00 and 9:00am. After nine, many stalls start packing up, and the main market only gets lively again in the evening. If you want both morning and evening, plan two separate visits.

blocks.text: Khao Phan Phak — The Must-Try of Laplae

blocks.html: If you come to Uttaradit and don't eat khao phan phak, you haven't really arrived. This dish comes from Laplae and has been passed down for over 100 years. The name has the word "rice" in it, but there isn't a single grain of steamed rice — the wrapper is made from rice flour spread thin over cloth above steam, then rolled around blanched vegetables, egg, or various fillings, and topped with a well-balanced dipping sauce. Eaten hot, it's soft and silky, light on the stomach but filling. A plate usually runs under 100 THB, and many shops start at just 20–30 THB.

items.name: Huen Mon Kaew Khao Phan Phak Laplae
items.blurb: Set in an old wooden house over 120 years old, run into its fourth generation, with more than 20 khao phan phak options — with egg, with yellow noodles, even with instant noodles. The big seller is the crispy wonton tam thai, sliced fried wonton at 40 THB a plate. The setting alone is part of the appeal.

items.name: Khao Phan Phak Indy
items.blurb: The shop out-of-towners know best, with plenty of reviews. They make khao phan phak several ways, including with egg and topped with larb, full-flavored for anyone who likes it punchy. Easy on the wallet at under 100 THB, easy to find, and easy to park.

items.name: Phop Laplae Khao Phan Phak
items.blurb: On In Jai Mee Road, on the right just before the Laplae town gate. They make khao phan phak fresh, one plate at a time, with several fillings to choose from, all down-to-earth and under 100 THB. Easy parking, a good stop before you head into Laplae old town.
items.meta: In Jai Mee Rd, Laplae district

items.name: Huen Khao Phan Phak Rim Khlong
items.blurb: A shop that took off on social media, with canal-side seating that's cool and relaxed. Hot khao phan phak with a well-balanced dipping sauce, plus parking. A good spot to settle in if you'd rather eat slowly and chat.

items.name: Khao Phan Phak Chao Fa Ham Kuman
items.blurb: Near the Chao Fa Ham Kuman monument in Fai Luang subdistrict. The standout is that they cook it in a clay pot, giving it an aroma the others don't have. It opens earlier than many shops, so it's good if you're up early and want khao phan phak as your first meal.

blocks.title: Getting the Most Out of Khao Phan Phak
blocks.html: Most khao phan phak shops make each plate fresh to order, so expect a short wait when it's busy. Order several fillings to share, and try something unusual like the yellow-noodle or instant-noodle version. You'll see why people in Laplae can eat it for breakfast every day.

blocks.text: Congee and Rice Porridge to Warm You Up

blocks.html: On days you want something hot and easy to slurp down, the congee and rice porridge spots in Uttaradit have regulars that open before dawn. Good for early starts or for eating before the market is in full swing.

items.name: Clay-Pot Pork Congee (in front of Friday Mall)
items.blurb: Open for over 20 years — they used to sell from a yellow cart in front of Khlong Pho Market and have now moved in front of Friday Mall, across from Amazon. Smooth pork congee simmered in a clay pot. Open 05:00–10:30 and again 15:00–21:30 (closed Saturday evening).

items.name: Jok Tua Tor, Khlong Pho Market Branch
items.blurb: A Khlong Pho Market regular, open early around 05:30–11:30. Good for a hot bowl to cap off breakfast after you've walked the market.

blocks.html: Breakfast in Uttaradit isn't just new-school cafes. The real thing the old coffee crowd still seeks out is old-school coffee, or kopi — brewed dark and sweet-creamy in the traditional way, eaten with patongko or sangkhaya toast. It's a fitting way to close out breakfast before you head off again.

items: Kopi Old-School Coffee (toward Wat Klang) — from the big Air intersection heading toward Wat Klang, on the right just before the temple. Seriously strong coffee with a full lineup of southern-style tea and coffee. Open daily 06:30–16:00.
Old-school coffee in the morning market — several vendors set up low tables inside Khlong Pho Market, brewing fresh for just a few baht a glass. Great paired with patongko.
New-school cafes in Laplae — if you want drip coffee or a chill place to sit, there are several new cafes around town, perfect after a khao phan phak meal.

blocks.title: Making the Most of One Morning
blocks.html: Start before dawn at Khlong Pho Market for patongko and soy milk, have a clay-pot congee to warm up, then drive 8 km to Laplae to hunt down khao phan phak. Finish with strong old-school coffee — you'll cover both the town's food and Laplae's in a single morning.

faq.q: What breakfast should you try in Uttaradit?
faq.a: Laplae's khao phan phak is the one you can't miss — a thin flour wrapper rolled around vegetables and egg, topped with dipping sauce, eaten hot, starting at 20–30 THB a plate. Beyond that there's patongko with soy milk at Khlong Pho Market, clay-pot congee, and strong old-school coffee.

faq.q: Where can you find khao phan phak in Uttaradit?
faq.a: Most of the famous shops are in Laplae district, about 8 km from town — like Huen Mon Kaew in a 120-plus-year-old wooden house, the well-reviewed Khao Phan Phak Indy, and Phop Laplae on In Jai Mee Road. Most open late-morning around 9am until evening.

faq.q: What time should you go to the Uttaradit morning market?
faq.a: The breakfast side of Khlong Pho Market has stalls open from around 5:30am, and it's best between 6:00 and 9:00am — after nine, many stalls start packing up. The main market gets lively again in the evening, roughly 3pm until dark.

Not at all. Many shops start at 20–30 THB a plate, and a filling meal per person usually comes in under 100 THB. Special items like the crispy wonton tam thai run around 40 THB. It's great-value local food.

faq.q: If you only have one morning, what should you eat first?
faq.a: Start at Khlong Pho Market in town before dawn for patongko, soy milk, and clay-pot congee, then drive out to Laplae for khao phan phak as the main event. Finish with old-school coffee — you'll cover both areas in a single morning.
